acceptance_checks: No valid fractal swing can exist without both a mapped point of interest and a qualifying Candle 2 or Candle 3 closure.
If Candle 2 already qualifies as the valid closure, the model must stop the delayed Candle 3 path instead of double-counting both.
No Candle 3 closure can qualify unless Candle 2 first failed to produce the valid reversal closure.
Midpoint and equilibrium refinement gates must be explicit and configurable whenever the draft claims to use them.
Lower-timeframe refinement must stay bar-close confirmed and remain gated behind the higher-timeframe and point-of-interest path.
The script must keep multi-timeframe requests finite and below the configured request budget.
Backtest results must include spread, slippage, commission, and fee assumptions before performance is treated as credible.
Historical execution must assume next-bar-open entry after a confirmed bar-close signal instead of intrabar lookahead fills.
If stop and target touch in the same bar, assume the stop prints first unless lower-timeframe replay evidence proves the target filled first.

alerts.condition: The fractal closure path fails before or after refinement.
alerts.name: fractal_invalidated

implementation_summary: First-pass Pine overlay draft for the TTrades fractal closure model using point-of-interest gating, Candle 2 or Candle 3 closure detection, midpoint and equilibrium refinement, and provisional lower-timeframe displacement confirmation.

Require the mapped point of interest and closure sequence to agree with the higher-timeframe directional idea.
Choose whether the fractal sequence needs intermediate-timeframe structure agreement in addition to higher-timeframe bias.
A Candle 2 closure requires a sweep of the prior candle and a close back inside its range.
If Candle 2 already qualifies as the valid reversal closure, stop the delayed Candle 3 path.

Provisional tolerance band for saying Candle 3 respected or disrespected the Candle 2 wick midpoint.
Require Candle 4 to retest and respect the correct half of Candle 3 for the refined continuation path.
Provisional tolerance band used when deciding whether Candle 4 respected the intended half of Candle 3.

open_implementation_questions.question: What body-overlap threshold is the best first numeric proxy for saying Candle 3 truly engulfed Candle 2 when Candle 2 is small or doji-like?
What is the first useful numeric tolerance for saying Candle 3 respected the Candle 2 midpoint or Candle 4 respected the correct half of Candle 3?
How should the fallback opposing-candle point of interest be ranked against clearer swing or fair-value-gap anchors?
What is the minimum lower-timeframe displacement strength needed before the refined fractal path is truly entry-ready?

pine_translation_hints: Prefer bar-close confirmation over intrabar discretion.
Keep lower-timeframe requests focused and finite.
Represent structure and invalidation as explicit state objects.

provisional_proxies.logic: Rank point-of-interest anchors by preferring swing highs or lows first, then fair value gap proxies, then fallback opposing candles only when no cleaner anchor exists.
Treat Candle 3 as a valid delayed closure only when its close exceeds the Candle 2 body by the configured engulf threshold in the new direction.
Use configurable tolerance bands for Candle 2 midpoint respect and Candle 3 correct-half respect until the narrative filters are grounded numerically.
Require a first-pass lower-timeframe impulse or protected-swing proxy after the qualifying closure before promoting the sequence into entry-ready state.

signal_pipeline.logic: Map the higher-timeframe point of interest first, then require higher-timeframe bias and optional intermediate-timeframe structure to support the fractal closure path.
signal_pipeline.name: Context and Point-of-Interest Gate

signal_pipeline.logic: Detect the Candle 2 sweep and close-back-inside event first and prefer that path whenever it already produces the valid reversal closure.
signal_pipeline.name: Candle 2 Reversal Closure Detection

signal_pipeline.logic: If Candle 2 does not qualify, require Candle 3 to close through the Candle 2 body in the new direction before validating the delayed closure path.
signal_pipeline.name: Candle 3 Delayed Closure Fallback

signal_pipeline.logic: Apply Candle 2 wick-midpoint respect when large-wick rejection exists, then apply Candle 3 equilibrium-half respect for the Candle 4 refinement path.
signal_pipeline.name: Midpoint and Equilibrium Refinement

signal_pipeline.logic: Require lower-timeframe displacement after the qualifying closure before treating the swing as refined and entry-ready.
signal_pipeline.name: Lower-Timeframe Displacement Gate

signal_pipeline.logic: Once refinement holds, project Candle 4 continuation and expansion in the new direction and invalidate the model when the closure or refinement path breaks first.
signal_pipeline.name: Candle 4 Expectation and Failure Management

transitions.condition: A valid point of interest is mapped and higher-timeframe context does not reject the setup.
A valid Candle 2 reversal closure appears at the point of interest.
Candle 2 does not qualify and Candle 3 closes through the Candle 2 body in the new direction.
The enabled midpoint or equilibrium refinement checks hold after the qualifying closure.
Lower-timeframe displacement confirms the refined path when that mode is enabled.
The closure path fails, the midpoint or half-respect filter breaks, or the lower-timeframe refinement never develops in the intended direction.

machine_checks: Detect close above previous high or below previous low
Detect sweep beyond previous high or low followed by close back inside the prior range
Store current bias mode as continuation or reversal
rules.name: Next-candle bias starts from how price closes relative to the previous candle range
pine_inputs_needed: sweep state relative to previous candle range

machine_checks: Mark prior-day high and low as reversal anchors
Measure whether the higher-timeframe candle sweeps a prior-day extreme and closes back inside or rejects from it
Require lower-timeframe confirmation before execution mode is active
rules.name: Reversal-day bias is framed from previous day highs or lows plus lower-timeframe confirmation

machine_checks: Compute equilibrium as midpoint of previous day range
Detect whether lower-timeframe closes remain on the correct side of equilibrium
Require continuation through the previous day directional objective
rules.name: Continuation-day bias uses prior candle closure plus equilibrium respect

machine_checks: Compute body size and opposing wick ratio
Classify whether the candle closes near its directional extreme or near its open
Switch expected target model based on small-wick versus large-wick classification
rules.name: Wick size filters whether the current candle supports expansion or reversion

machine_checks: Store higher-timeframe bias as a state variable
Reject lower-timeframe execution signals that oppose the active bias
Allow configurable execution timeframe mapping by session or user selection
rules.name: Higher-timeframe bias filters all lower-timeframe entries
pine_inputs_needed: session bucket or preferred execution window

open_questions: What is the first useful numeric tolerance for saying Candle 3 respected versus disrespected the Candle 2 wick midpoint?
How should the fallback opposing-candle point of interest be ranked against clearer swing or fair-value-gap anchors?

machine_checks: Detect sweep beyond the previous candle high or low
Require the Candle 2 close to finish back inside the previous candle range
Classify the event as bullish or bearish based on which side was swept and reclaimed
rules.name: A Candle 2 closure is always a reversal closure that sweeps the previous candle and closes back inside its range

machine_checks: Require a mapped point of interest before a Candle 2 closure can become actionable
Allow a fallback opposing-candle anchor only when no clearer higher-timeframe point of interest exists
Reject Candle 2 events that form without higher-timeframe alignment
rules.name: A Candle 2 closure is only valid when it forms at a higher-timeframe point of interest

machine_checks: Store the Candle 2 range after a valid reversal closure appears
Detect whether Candle 3 closes beyond Candle 2 in the new direction
Invalidate the sequence when Candle 3 cannot confirm the directional handoff
rules.name: A valid Candle 2 closure should hand off to Candle 3 continuation in the new direction

machine_checks: Compute the Candle 2 wick midpoint from the rejection candle
Track whether Candle 3 respects the midpoint in the direction of the reversal
Downgrade the setup when midpoint respect fails before continuation develops
rules.name: Large-wick Candle 2 closures should keep Candle 3 above or below the wick midpoint to remain valid

open_questions: What body-overlap threshold is the best first numeric proxy for saying Candle 3 truly engulfed Candle 2 when Candle 2 is very small or doji-like?
What is the first useful numeric tolerance for saying Candle 4 respected the correct half of Candle 3 and produced enough lower-timeframe displacement to justify entry refinement?

machine_checks: Reject the sequence if Candle 2 already qualifies as a valid Candle 2 reversal closure
Measure the Candle 2 body and require Candle 3 to close through it in the new direction
Emit a bullish or bearish Candle 3 closure state only after the delayed engulfing close appears
rules.name: A Candle 3 closure confirms the move when Candle 2 fails to produce the earlier reversal closure

machine_checks: Require a mapped point of interest before a Candle 3 closure can become actionable
Require higher-timeframe directional agreement before promoting the Candle 3 event into a valid swing
Ignore Candle 3 body-engulfing closes that occur in random mid-range locations
rules.name: A Candle 3 closure only matters when it appears at the mapped point of interest and inside the higher-timeframe idea

machine_checks: Measure Candle 3 equilibrium from wick high to wick low
Require Candle 4 to trade back into the correct half of Candle 3 for the equilibrium-refinement path
Flag loss of refinement when Candle 4 breaks through the wrong side of Candle 3 equilibrium before expansion confirms
rules.name: After a valid Candle 3 closure, Candle 4 should respect the correct half of Candle 3's range

machine_checks: Require both a point of interest and a qualifying closure before validating a swing
Allow either Candle 2 or Candle 3 to satisfy the closure requirement, but never neither
Hold the sequence in pending state until lower-timeframe displacement confirms the refined entry path
rules.name: No swing point is valid without both the point of interest and the closure event

open_questions: What is the best first explicit proxy for CISD so intermediate-timeframe confirmation can be scored without discretionary chart reading?
How many alignment failures across the stack should immediately cancel a setup instead of merely downgrading it?

machine_checks: Require a higher-timeframe directional classification before evaluating lower-timeframe entries
Reject lower-timeframe continuation signals that directly oppose the higher-timeframe bias
Downgrade all lower-timeframe setups when the higher timeframe is still unresolved consolidation
rules.name: The higher timeframe sets the directional bias and lower timeframes should not override it on their own

machine_checks: Require an intermediate-timeframe point of interest that agrees with higher-timeframe direction
Require a directional closure or CISD before promoting the setup to execution-ready state
Flag the setup as pending when higher-timeframe bias exists but intermediate-timeframe structure is still missing
rules.name: The intermediate timeframe must confirm the higher-timeframe bias with structure, a point of interest, and a directional closure

machine_checks: Gate lower-timeframe entry logic behind an explicit higher-plus-intermediate alignment flag
Treat lower-timeframe structure as execution refinement instead of independent direction selection
Invalidate the refined entry when lower-timeframe structure immediately breaks against the aligned thesis
rules.name: The lower timeframe is for entry precision only after the higher and intermediate timeframes are already aligned
pine_inputs_needed: alignment flag between higher and intermediate timeframes

machine_checks: Require at least two expansion-supporting timeframe flags for the clean-trend classification
Elevate the setup quality when all three monitored timeframes align
Downgrade or defer the setup when any parent timeframe prints a non-expansion-supporting candle
rules.name: A clean trend requires aligned expansion-supporting candles across at least two timeframes

open_questions: What numeric tolerance around the 0.5 line should count as valid equilibrium respect versus a true close-through failure?
How should multiple points of interest inside the respected half be ranked before lower-timeframe confirmation appears?

machine_checks: Compute equilibrium as the midpoint between wick high and wick low
Reject body-only midpoint calculations for this topic
Persist the selected midpoint until the reference range is intentionally replaced
rules.name: Equilibrium is measured from wick high to wick low, not from candle bodies

machine_checks: Track whether price is holding in the correct half of the reference range
Flag loss of continuation bias when closes move through the wrong side of equilibrium
Keep the continuation bias active only while the expected half remains respected
rules.name: In expansion conditions, respect of the correct half of the range defines the directional bias

machine_checks: Project the previous day's equilibrium into the new session
Reject continuation when lower-timeframe closes occur beyond equilibrium in the wrong direction
Allow minor probing around the midpoint only until the close-based failure condition appears
rules.name: A continuation day is framed from the previous day's equilibrium and confirmed by lower-timeframe closes that stay on the correct side

machine_checks: Require both a point of interest and lower-timeframe confirmation before promoting an equilibrium reaction into an entry setup
Allow fallback to newly created liquidity only if it remains inside the respected half of the range
Mark the setup as context-only when equilibrium is respected but no confirmation appears
rules.name: Equilibrium becomes tradable when the respected half also contains a point of interest and lower-timeframe confirmation

open_questions: What numeric ratio should separate a small opposing run from a large opposing wick across the main timeframe pairs?
How close to the open should a candle finish before it is treated as a reversal-style candle instead of an expansion candle?

machine_checks: Compute the wick opposite the candle direction and compare it against the body
Require the close to finish near the directional extreme rather than near the open
Classify the candle as expansion-supporting only when the opposing wick remains small relative to the full range
rules.name: A small opposing wick with a large body supports expansion in the candle direction

machine_checks: Classify candles with dominant opposing wicks as poor expansion candidates
Downgrade continuation expectations when the close finishes too close to the open
Switch the target model toward the open or nearby liquidity after a large opposing run
rules.name: A large opposing wick with a smaller body favors reversion toward the open or nearby liquidity

machine_checks: Compute the wick midpoint from the body edge to the wick extreme
Track whether subsequent closes remain on the respected side of the midpoint
Flip the wick state from respected to disrespected once a close breaches the midpoint
rules.name: Respect or disrespect of the wick midpoint determines whether rejection is holding or failing

machine_checks: Classify the higher-timeframe candle first as expansion-supporting or reversal-leaning based on wick behavior
Gate lower-timeframe expansion reads on the higher-timeframe wick classification
Downgrade lower-timeframe continuation setups when the parent candle shows large opposing rejection
rules.name: Higher-timeframe wick behavior should govern whether lower-timeframe structure is read as expansion, reversal, or range
